title: sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's check can only ever report one dropped country per future per night by construction, and three non-primary countries across two futures have sat uncaught for as long as two weeks as a result
statement: practice/src/practice/foreknown/run.py line 112-113 computes `dropped = sorted(sources.primary_iso3(properties) - set(known.get("iso3") or []))`, and `sources.primary_iso3` (practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py, lines 50-57) returns `{value} if value else set()` for the feed's single top-level `properties.iso3` string -- a set of at most one element, always. The subtraction can therefore never produce more than one dropped country per future per night, regardless of how many are actually missing from the committed record; this is a property of the check's return type, not of the data it has seen so far. Two GDACS-sourced OPEN futures currently hold non-primary countries that this construction cannot see. foreknown/registry.json's gdacs-dr-1018332 (drought, announced 2026-08-08T17:40:13+00:00) shows a REVISED event at 2026-08-18T05:59:34+00:00 whose `where`/`what` diff adds 'Ireland' and 'Netherlands' to the tracked text -- confirmed against foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-18/gdacs.json's raw feature: `affectedcountries` includes IRL and NLD from that night onward (also present in foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-30/gdacs.json and .../2026-09-01/gdacs.json, unbroken). The future's committed `iso3` array, read from foreknown/registry.json today, is 28 entries -- ALB, AUT, BEL, BGR, BIH, BLR, CHE, CZE, DEU, DNK, ESP, FRA, HRV, HUN, ITA, LIE, LUX, MCO, MKD, MNE, POL, ROU, SMR, SRB, SVK, SVN, SWE, UKR -- IRL and NLD are absent from it, and unlike an earlier where-diff on the same future (2026-08-31T11:49:28+00:00, which re-adds 'Sweden' and 'San Marino' after a temporary absence from the raw feed) SWE and SMR are both already in the committed array, so that second event names no new gap; IRL and NLD are the only two of the future's ever-named countries that never entered `iso3` at all. Fifteen nights later (foreknown/reaction/readings/2026-09-01.json, the newest reading), this future's `iso3` field mirrors the same 28-country list with `unmapped_iso3: []` -- IRL and NLD are not merely unmapped, they are not present to be checked, and foreknown/reaction/iso3-fips.json's 85 entries confirm neither has a crosswalk row (a second, independent gap: even a corrected registry could not resolve either to a fips code today). Every foreknown/snapshots/<date>/run.json from 2026-08-18 through 2026-09-01 that this observation checked (18, 19, 28, 30, 31, 09-01) shows `primary_iso3_dropped` never once naming gdacs-dr-1018332/IRL or /NLD, because this future's singular `properties.iso3` has read 'ALB' or 'AUT' throughout that whole span -- both already committed, so the one-slot check finds nothing to report even while two real gaps sit beside it. The same shape recurred this week on a second future: gdacs-dr-1027449 (drought, first NOTARIZED 2026-08-18T05:59:34+00:00, iso3 committed as BLZ, GTM, HND, MEX, NIC, SLV) shows a REVISED event at 2026-08-31T11:49:28+00:00 adding both 'The Bahamas' and 'Cuba' to `where`/`what` in the same diff; foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-31/gdacs.json and .../2026-09-01/gdacs.json both show `affectedcountries` grown from 6 to 8 (BHS, BLZ, CUB, GTM, HND, MEX, NIC, SLV) with the feed's singular `properties.iso3` now reading 'BHS'. Because BHS happens to be the new primary, the check does catch it -- foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-31/run.json and .../2026-09-01/run.json both list `{"future": "gdacs-dr-1027449", "dropped_iso3": ["BHS"]}` -- but CUB, added in the identical event by the identical mechanism, is invisible to the same check because it never became the primary reporting position; it is absent from committed `iso3` and from foreknown/reaction/readings/2026-09-01.json's `iso3` field for this future exactly as IRL/NLD are, even though CUB, unlike BHS, does have a crosswalk row (iso3-fips.json: CUB -> fips CU) and so is resolvable today if the registry only carried it.
method: Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/run.py's primary_iso3_dropped computation (lines 97-116) and practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py's primary_iso3 function (lines 50-57) to establish that the subtraction is against a singleton set by construction. Scanned foreknown/registry.json's futures for every GDACS-sourced history entry with a `where` change (python3 json load, one pass over all history lists, comparing comma-split country-name sets between each REVISED event's `from`/`to`) and filtered for diffs adding two or more countries in one event: found gdacs-dr-1018332 (2026-08-18, adds Ireland/Netherlands; 2026-08-31, adds Sweden/San Marino) and gdacs-dr-1027449 (2026-08-31, adds The Bahamas/Cuba). For each, read the future's committed `iso3` array from foreknown/registry.json and diffed it against every named country to identify which additions never entered the array. Cross-checked committed `iso3` against the raw feed for the same event id in foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-17/gdacs.json, .../2026-08-18/gdacs.json, .../2026-08-30/gdacs.json and .../2026-08-31/gdacs.json (properties.affectedcountries and properties.iso3 read directly, python3 json load) to confirm IRL/NLD/CUB's presence in affectedcountries from their respective REVISED dates onward and that SWE/SMR were already committed (ruling them out as a gap). Scanned foreknown/snapshots/<date>/run.json's `primary_iso3_dropped` field for 2026-08-18, 19, 28, 30, 31 and 2026-09-01 for both future ids to confirm the sensor never named IRL, NLD, or CUB in any of those nights. Read foreknown/reaction/readings/2026-09-01.json's `futures` entries for both future ids (their committed `iso3`, `unmapped_iso3` and `fips` fields) and foreknown/reaction/iso3-fips.json's 85 `entries` for IRL, NLD, SWE, SMR, CUB and BHS to establish which of the missing countries do and do not have a crosswalk row today. No live fetch; every figure above is read from committed repository files as they stand in this checkout.

figures.sensor_return_type: sources.primary_iso3 returns a set of size 0 or 1, never more, by its own implementation

worth_watching_because: sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's own text describes its job in general terms -- 'a coverage gap in a country field' -- and its three prior reviews (2026-08-20 ERI, 2026-08-24 CHN, 2026-08-25 the CHN case closing without correction) all read as confirmations that the mechanism (iso3 is not a futures.py TRACKED_FIELD, so it never re-syncs once a future is notarized) is real and recurring. Every one of those confirmed cases, though, happened to be caught because the newly-added country also became the feed's singular reporting position. This observation is the first case where the same mechanism produced a country that the check structurally cannot report -- not because the case is rarer or newer, but because `primary_iso3` can only ever hold one value and a `where`-changing event can add more than one country at once, which the registry's own history shows happening on both 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-31. IRL and NLD have now sat uncaught for fifteen consecutive nights on a future the sensor is actively running against every night; CUB entered the identical night, the identical event, and the identical future-type as a case the sensor did catch (BHS), which makes it a clean same-night natural control showing the check's own blind spot rather than a separately-caused gap. Whether the fix is to check the full affectedcountries union rather than only the primary field (which would also close the registry-side gap the 2026-08-20/24/25 reviews already named, since `iso3` still is not a TRACKED_FIELD) is a design question for the sensor's own maintainer -- diagnosing that a promoted, running sensor's return type makes it incapable of ever reporting more than one gap per future per night is a fact about the committed code, not a redesign of it.
left_alone: Not changing run.py's primary_iso3_dropped computation or sources.py's primary_iso3 function -- widening the check to compare the full affectedcountries union against committed iso3, rather than only the singular field, is a real change to a PROMOTED sensor's running behaviour (it would very likely also surface IRL, NLD and CUB retroactively the next time it runs, and possibly other cases this observation did not go looking for), which is a decision for sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's own review chain and its maintainer, not something one same-night natural-control instance settles by itself. Added this finding as a new dated review entry on sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json instead, alongside this observation, following the pattern its own three prior reviews already set. Not adding IRL, NLD or BHS to foreknown/reaction/iso3-fips.json -- the crosswalk's own method note says every entry is checked against GDELT's issuing FIPS.country.txt, which this observation did not fetch; recording that three specific countries are absent from an 85-entry, hand-authored, 2026-08-08 crosswalk is a fact about today's coverage, not a verified correction to it. Not touching the other PROPOSED sensors tonight: lead-time-pathway-idle is unchanged at 7 of the 10 FORECAST-kind resolutions its test_rule waits for (four FORECAST futures are now OPEN -- nhc-al052026, nhc-ep112026, nhc-ep122026, nhc-ep132026 -- none yet resolved); registry-stall and source-reconfirmation-blind-spot both still carry open reviews asking for a firing-rule redesign, and no register has gone stale (foreknown/snapshots, foreknown/reaction/snapshots, darkocean/snapshots and memoryhole/readings are all within 1 day of yesterday, 2026-08-31/2026-09-01); resolution-reappearance-coverage's only live case (gdacs-tc-1001305) is still OPEN as of foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-01/run.json and has not closed a second time. Not writing a memoryhole/verdicts file -- memoryhole/readings/2026-08-31.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 41 entries.
